realm.name: product:read
realm.description: Read products.

realm.name: product:write
realm.description: Create and modify products.

realm.name: journey:read
realm.description: View call frequencies and journey plans (Journey module).

realm.name: visit:read
realm.description: View visits and where they were checked in (Visit module).

realm.name: visit:write
realm.description: Check in at an outlet and work a visit (Visit module).

realm.name: journey:annotate
realm.description: Report on a round: not-visited reasons, unplanned calls, moves (Journey module).

realm.name: journey:write
realm.description: Set call frequencies and generate journey plans (Journey module).

realm.name: role:read
realm.description: View roles. Held here so the second tenant can be asked what roles it has — which is how per-tenant role seeding (IAM-06) is provable rather than assumed.

realm.name: orgunit:read
realm.description: View the sales hierarchy. Held here for the same reason as role:read — a second tenant that cannot be asked what it sees cannot demonstrate that it sees only its own (ORG-01).

realm.name: orgunit:write
realm.description: Edit the sales hierarchy. Held by the second tenant so that reaching for another tenant's unit is refused by the query filter (404) rather than by the permission check (403) — otherwise the isolation test passes without isolation.

realm.name: position:read
realm.description: View positions. Held so per-tenant org staffing can be asked about rather than assumed (ORG-02).

realm.name: position:write
realm.description: Edit positions. Held for the same reason as orgunit:write — a cross-tenant attempt must be refused by the query filter, not by the permission check.

realm.name: outlet:read
realm.description: View outlets. Held so the second tenant can be asked what it sees (OUT-01).

realm.name: outlet:write
realm.description: Edit outlets. Held for the same reason as orgunit:write — a cross-tenant attempt must be refused by the query filter (404), not by the permission check (403).

realm.name: channel:read
realm.description: View channels. Held so per-tenant classification vocabularies can be shown to be separate.

realm.name: channel:write
realm.description: Create channels. The second tenant needs to be able to build its own outlets — a tenant that cannot create data cannot demonstrate that another tenant is unable to reach it.

realm.name: territory:read
realm.description: View territories. Held so the second tenant can be asked what it sees (ORG-03).

realm.name: territory:write
realm.description: Edit territories. Held so a cross-tenant attempt is refused by the query filter (404), not by the permission check (403).

realm.name: config:read
realm.description: View custom-field definitions. Held so per-tenant catalogues can be shown to be separate (CFG-01).

realm.name: config:write
realm.description: Define custom fields. The second tenant needs its own catalogue to demonstrate that one tenant's definitions never validate another's values.

clients.name: FieldKit web (Next.js)
clients.description: Same client id as the first realm — clients are realm-scoped, so this is a different client that happens to share a name.

clients.name: Impostor (test fixture — asserts the wrong tenant)
clients.description: Exists to be refused: its hardcoded tenant claim names the FIRST tenant, so it mints real signatures from a trusted issuer for someone else's tenant. See realms/README.md. Never enable a client like this in a real realm.
